name: HT16K33 4-digit 7-segment display (I2C backpack)
description: Four-digit 0.56" 7-segment LED display with centre colon, driven by a Holtek HT16K33 RAM-mapped LED controller over I2C (up to 400 kHz). 16-step dimming, hardware blink, address 0x70-0x77 set by solder jumpers A0-A2. HT16K33 supply 4.5-5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit 0.56" 4-Digit 7-Segment Display w/ I2C Backpack (product 878 red; 879-881, 1002 other colours; STEMMA QT revision), 4-pin header +, -, D, C.
eli5: Four big glowing digits that show numbers your board sends over just two wires.

pins.description: VCC / VDD supply for the HT16K33 and LEDs, 5 V (chip spec 4.5-5.5 V); the 10 kOhm SDA/SCL pull-ups go to this pin

pins.name: D
pins.description: I2C data (SDA), 10 kOhm pull-up to + on the backpack

pins.name: C
pins.description: I2C clock (SCL), 10 kOhm pull-up to + on the backpack

buildNotes: Init sequence from the datasheet: 0x21 (oscillator on), 0xE0|brightness (0-15), then 0x81 (display on, no blink). At power-up the oscillator is stopped and the display is off, so nothing lights until these are sent.

Write display RAM with one I2C write: 0x00 followed by the data bytes. On this backpack the digits are RAM bytes 0, 2, 6 and 8 (left to right) and byte 4 bit 1 (0x02) is the centre colon. Segment bits: bit0 = a ... bit6 = g, bit7 = decimal point.

The board's 10 kOhm SDA/SCL pull-ups go to the + pin. With + on 5 V the bus idles at 5 V, which is above an ESP32's or Pico's 3.6 V pin limit: use a bidirectional I2C level shifter (e.g. BSS138 type) between a 3.3 V board and the backpack. Adafruit reports + on 3.3 V also works (dimmer, below the HT16K33's 4.5 V spec).
Default address 0x70; solder A0/A1/A2 jumpers closed to add 1/2/4 (0x71-0x77) for up to eight displays on one bus.
All segments lit at full brightness draws on the order of 100 mA from +: power it from the 5 V (VBUS/VIN) pin, not a GPIO.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ht16k33seg import HT16K33Seg

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=400000)
disp = HT16K33Seg(i2c, 0x70)
value = -8.75
disp.number(value, 2)
print('shown %.2f' % value)
while True:
    time.sleep(1)

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (2 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
